gen.title: How amendments became the Bill of Rights
gen.orderNote: Steps follow the order ideas appear in the text from debate to adoption

steps.label: tyranny by the central government
steps.quote: its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny by the central government
steps.orderHint: Arrange in the order the document presents them

steps.label: bill of rights
steps.quote: They demanded a "bill of rights" that would spell out the immunities of individual citizens.
steps.orderHint: Arrange in the order the document presents them

steps.label: asked for such amendments
steps.quote: Several state conventions in their formal ratification of the Constitution asked for such amendments
steps.orderHint: Arrange in the order the document presents them

steps.label: proposed to the state legislatures
steps.quote: On September 25, 1789, the First Congress of the United States therefore proposed to the state legislatures 12 amendments to the Constitution
steps.orderHint: Arrange in the order the document presents them

steps.label: Articles 3 to 12
steps.quote: Articles 3 to 12, ratified December 15, 1791, by three-fourths of the state legislatures, constitute the first 10 amendments
steps.orderHint: Arrange in the order the document presents them
